name: Freelance deliverable
summary: A digital work product handed over privately, with proof of delivery — and no marketplace fee.
description: A client commissions a digital deliverable — a design file, a production cut, a dataset, an access credential — from an independent professional. The hand-off travels an encrypted channel straight between the two of them, and a fingerprint of the file is recorded as proof it arrived. Both sides are bonded, so the client's payment and the freelancer's delivery secure each other; the freelancer's catalogue can price a fixed fee or by the hour. No marketplace takes a cut.

faq.question: Where does the work come from?
faq.answer: From buyers who find you on Discover and from clients you bring. You publish what you offer; a buyer commits to it directly. No platform holds the relationship.

faq.question: What do I put up, and what do I get back?
faq.answer: A bond of twice the price of the work, in the token the trade uses. It is refunded whole when the buyer resolves, in the same transaction that pays you.

faq.question: What if the client never signs off?
faq.answer: Nothing moves for either side. The client's own bond, twice the price, stays locked with yours. Deliver, attest what you delivered, and put any shortfall right before resolution; a client who walks away pays for it too.
